unite_adi: REGULAR UPPER SECONDARY-YEAR 11-LEVEL: B1.3 THEME 7: LIFE IN NATURE & GLOBAL PROBLEMS

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students will explore globalisation and environmental issues, focusing on global problems such as urbanisation, climate change, and inequality, their impacts, and possible solutions. They will research the effects of globalisation on cultural exchange and the standard of living, analyse environmental challenges such as pollution and melting ice caps, and suggest solutions such as recycling, zero-waste practices, and policies for sustainability. Each student will write a short report explaining one global problem and one environmental issue, create a visual aid (poster or presentation) to represent the topics, and role-play as policymakers or environmentalists presenting solutions. The project will be presented in class. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''life in nature and global problems with its components such as globalisation, problems and solutions; environmental issues and solutions'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student of in an upper secondary school in year 11 may know what globalisation, problems and solutions; environmental issues and solutions mean in their own language as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in another language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students of an upper secondary school in year 11, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''life in nature and global problems'' in English from previous themes and/or years such as ''renewable resources, non-renewable resources, habitat destruction, global warming, climate change, to be conscious, to raise awareness,'' and also some structures such as ''Renewable resources that include solar and wind energy will be necessary for sustainable development. People will need to take precautions, so they can protect wildlife from habitat destruction in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in an upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''globalisation, problems and solutions; environmental issues and solutions'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a contextual poster or a large picture could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss the poster and/or the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To talk about global environmental problems, discuss their causes and solutions in English by using the target vocabulary. Activity 1: Problem-Solution Discussion: Environmental Issues The teacher organises students into small groups and assigns each group a global problem, such as deforestation or pollution. Using target vocabulary such as ''ecosystem, contamination, to cut down on, and to reuse'' along with grammar structures such as ''which, that, and so'', students discuss the problem, its causes, and potential solutions. Each group creates a plan, such as: ''Deforestation, which leads to habitat loss and climate change, needs immediate action. We recommend reducing the use of paper, which comes from trees, and encouraging practices such as reusing and recycling materials to conserve forests. To solve this, raising awareness so people understand the impact of their consumption habits is crucial''. Groups then present their plans, and the teacher provides feedback on vocabulary usage and grammatical accuracy. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To help students identify and categorise geographical features, environmental issues, and solutions in English by using target vocabulary. Activity 1: Categorize and Match: Environmental Awareness The teacher shows flashcards featuring geographical features such as ''beach, forest, and glacier'' and asks students to name them aloud, repeating the words for clarity. Next, s/he gives a worksheet with vocabulary items such as ''ozone layer, climate change, and to recycle'' where students categorise the words under ''Geographical Features'', ''Environmental Issues'', and ''Solutions''. For example, they match ''forest'' to ''Geographical Features'', ''climate change'' to ''Environmental Issues'', and ''to recycle'' to ''Solutions''. After completing the task, students read their matches aloud. The teacher listens, provides feedback, and corrects any misplacements. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
